title: Paver Patio Calculator
metaDescription: Estimate pavers, compacted base in cubic yards and tons, bedding sand, and edge restraint for a patio, walkway, or driveway, with ICPI base depths.
secondaryKeywords: how many pavers per square foot
how much paver base do i need
how deep should paver base be
intent: Estimate pavers, compacted base, bedding sand, and edge restraint for a patio or walkway.
registerRow: Keyword Register: paver calculator (Volume 2, Competition ease 3, Ad value 3, Fit 5, Priority 18)
intro: Enter your patio size and paver size to get the number of pavers to buy, plus the compacted gravel base and bedding sand underneath. Pick patio or driveway and your soil type, and the base depth is set from ICPI's published construction guide.
chartTitle: Base gravel needed at each ICPI depth option (tons)
uniqueAddition: Use and soil selector that sets the ICPI Tech Spec 2 base depth (4 in patio or 6 in driveway, plus 2 to 4 in for poor soil) and returns base tons and bedding sand together; the chart compares base tons at every ICPI depth option, and page.md adds a pavers-per-square-foot table for common sizes and a base depth recipe table.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.label: Patio shape
inputs.help: For an L-shape, split it into two rectangles and add the results.

inputs.name: length
inputs.label: Length
inputs.help: 1 to 100 ft. Use decimals for inches (12 ft 6 in = 12.5).

inputs.name: diameter
inputs.label: Diameter
inputs.help: 1 to 100 ft, measured straight across the circle.

inputs.name: perimeter
inputs.label: Edge length (optional)
inputs.help: Total length of open edges that need edge restraint. Leave blank to skip.

inputs.name: paverLength
inputs.label: Paver length
inputs.help: 4 to 24 in. The face size from the label (a common brick paver is 4 x 8 in).

inputs.name: use
inputs.label: What will it carry?
inputs.help: Sets the minimum compacted base depth from ICPI Tech Spec 2.

inputs.name: soil
inputs.label: Soil condition

options.label: Cold climate, wet, or weak soil

inputs.help: ICPI calls for a base 2 to 4 in thicker in cold climates or on continually wet or weak soil.

inputs.name: extraBase
inputs.label: Extra base for poor soil
inputs.help: 2 to 4 in, the range ICPI gives. Use more for colder or softer ground.

inputs.name: jointWidth
inputs.label: Joint width
inputs.help: 0 to 0.5 in. ICPI calls for joints of 1/16 to 3/16 in; 0.125 = 1/8 in. Use 0 if your size already includes spacer bars.

inputs.name: sandDepth
inputs.label: Bedding sand depth
inputs.help: 0.5 to 2 in. ICPI specifies 1 in nominal, screeded and not compacted.

inputs.name: density
inputs.label: Base density
inputs.help: 1.0 to 2.0. Estimate only (not verified): ask your supplier for the weight of their base material and enter it here.

inputs.name: waste
inputs.label: Paver waste
inputs.help: 0 to 20%. Extra for cuts and breakage. 5% is our starting estimate, not a published figure; patterns with lots of cuts (herringbone, curves) need more.

sources.title: ICPI Tech Spec 2: Construction of Interlocking Concrete Pavements, revised February 2020 (Interlocking Concrete Pavement Institute): minimum compacted base 4 in for patios and walks and 6 in for residential driveways over well-drained soil, 2 to 4 in thicker in cold, wet, or weak soil; bedding sand 1 in nominal uncompacted; joint width 1/16 to 3/16 in
CMHA resource page PAV-TEC-010 (Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, the successor organization to ICPI)
